replication.target_description: Study 1: independent high-anchor Studio 97 versus low-anchor Studio 17 comparison of restaurant meal willingness-to-pay estimates, Table 1, primary outlier-excluded analysis.

n.location: p.5, Table 1, Restaurant row, High n and Low n columns
n.sample_role: Participants contributing one restaurant estimate each to the independent two-group test; sum of mutually exclusive final High and Low anchor groups.
n.exclusions: Item-specific outliers more than 1.5 IQR from the extreme of the IQR excluded; p.4 reports 5.56% across all observations, not a restaurant-specific percentage. Recruitment N=144 is not used as analytic N.

p.quote: the low anchor group but the difference fell far short of ... statistical significance (p = .26)

reported_success.quote: We were unable to find any statistically ... significant difference in price estimations between ... Studio 17 and Studio 97.

notes: Identity independently confirmed from title page and closing citation: Shanks, Barbieri-Hermitte and Vadillo (2020), Do Incidental Environmental Anchors Bias Consumers’ Price Estimations?, Collabra: Psychology 6(1):19, DOI 10.1525/collabra.310; labelled ORIGINAL RESEARCH REPORT. Supplied canonical text contains all 15 article pages, methods, results, tables and references, rather than an abstract-only excerpt. No PDF path supplied; no PDF rendered. Target selected by supplied study identifier, restaurant outcome, and the article’s explicit connection to Critcher and Gilovich Study 3 and Dogerlioglu-Demir and Koçaş Study 1 (p.3 Study 1 aims, p.5 discussion, p.7 Study 3). Business-name wording is interpreted in that explicit original-study context as Studio 97 versus Studio 17, rather than Tap 92 versus Tap 42. Repeated indistinguishable locators receive the same source-supported restaurant test; no assignment by row order or numeric matching. Study 2 locator p.5 introduces its restaurant design; its results are on p.6. Analytic N derivation: 67 + 69 = 136. High and Low are exclusive randomized anchor conditions for the same restaurant item, not repeated observations to be pooled across items. Table 1 Restaurant: Cohen’s d 0.11, t 0.65, df 134, BF+0 0.33; requested effect-size field is unassigned and remains a placeholder. Unassigned original and effect-size fields are placeholders only.
